title: An Approximate Solution to the Minimum Vertex Cover Problem: The Salvador Algorithm
content: Minimum Vertex Cover has a classical linear-time ratio of 2, and under the Unique Games Conjecture no polynomial-time algorithm achieves a fixed ratio below 2 unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. We present version 0.1.4 of Salvador, a linear-time ensemble of seventeen strategies, numbered in the order in which they are computed: twelve base strategies (component amplification before a maximal matching, the maximal matching itself, degree and weight heuristics, reductions to auxiliary problems that are solved exactly, a decomposition into bipartite layers, a weighted subdivision reduction and a bounded-treewidth dynamic program), followed by five improvers (a union pass, local search, reduce-and-search, consensus forcing and a swap-maximize refinement). We prove that every strategy runs in $O((n+m)\,\alpha(n))$ time, and that the returned cover has at most 2$\tau$-r vertices, where $r$ is the number of components with an edge, so the ratio is at most 1.999999999 whenever $\tau\le10^{9}r$. We prove exactness or a bounded ratio on several classes of graphs, among them every bipartite graph on which the Hopcroft–Karp phases of the layer strategy reach a maximum matching, and we give a per-instance certificate: a cover with at most $2L-|M|$ vertices, for a lower bound \(L\le\tau\) and the maximal matching $M$, is within ratio 3/2 on that instance. In a reproducible suite the returned cover satisfies \(|C|\le2\tau-|M|\) on all 291 tested graphs with a known optimum and is certified on the six without one, although single strategies violate it; on the 68 DIMACS clique complements it is never worse than Hvala and optimal on 37 instances against 18. Whether \(|C|\le2\tau-|M|\) holds on every graph is stated as a conjecture: a proof would give a linear-time 3/2-approximation and would refute the Unique Games Conjecture unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$.
